items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: I play, have performed almost exclusively with the guys who wrote the music. So it just doesn’t come up. With Russell, with Shelly and with Stephanie of course.

ctx.x: Wow. That’s sort of a specialized genre but over the years can you articulate what makes for a valuable piano accompanist?

Well because I do songs that were already arranged by the composers it’s not necessarily an issue because the usual answer to that would be someone who doesn’t overplay, someone who doesn’t rush. But I play, have performed almost exclusively with the guys who wrote the music. So it just doesn’t come up. With Russell, with Shelly and with Stephanie of course. So it’s completely natural. It’s difficult to do it with another person. Songs that I might not think are terribly difficult somebody, I tried to do them…

Are you mostly pleased with what jazz critics write about your work and you? I’m going to give you one that just — I spotted in a review in “Jazz Times.” “Intellectual jazz lab dedicated to the dissection of the human condition.”
